source_row.stem: During certain high-risk surgical procedures, double gloving is recommended, and a new surgical resident assumes this is done mainly to slow the surgeon down and encourage more careful movements. Double gloving is instead recommended primarily to:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Deliberately slow down the pace of the surgical procedure being performed, similar to what the new resident is currently assuming is the purpose of this practice","B":"Fully replace the need for any other personal protective equipment worn during the procedure, which is not the actual purpose of this particular practice","C":"Improve fine motor dexterity compared with wearing only a single pair of gloves, which is not the actual reason this practice is recommended","D":"Provide an additional barrier of protection, reducing exposure risk if the outer glove is punctured, rather than intentionally slowing the surgeon down as the resident is currently assuming"}}
source_row.rationale: Double gloving during high-risk surgical procedures provides an additional barrier of protection, reducing the risk of blood/body fluid exposure if the outer glove is punctured.
